sourcedFrom: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document (NOT PRINTED)
cleanIntro: A modular titanium .30 can that runs either 9 inches with the front module fitted or 7 inches without it, on a 5/8x24 direct thread. Eight STifle baffles live in it — six in the main tube and two in the front module — and it is user-serviceable end to end except for the muzzle-threaded end of the tube, which is fixed. Banish rates it .17 through .300 Weatherby and asks for a clean every 50 to 100 rounds.

steps.title: Clear the host firearm, and use ITS manual to do it
steps.action: Unload the rifle and open the action so the chamber is visibly clear before the can is touched. Banish deliberately does not print a clearing procedure — it sends you to your own firearm's manual, because a .30 can goes on everything from a bolt gun to an AR-10 and each clears differently.
steps.prose: That referral is the manual's own words and it is not boilerplate. A guide for the suppressor cannot know your action.
steps.quote: If you are at all unsure as to the proper procedures to ensure that your firearm is unloaded, please consult your firearm user’s manual/instructions and/or contact a properly licensed dealer or the manufacturer of your firearm.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: The host firearm's own manual is the clearing authority, not this one.

steps.title: Banish 30 ceiling — .300 WBY MAG on a 24 inch barrel
steps.action: Check the host cartridge and the barrel length together, because Banish states them as one limit: rated up to .300 WBY MAG with a 24 inch barrel, limited full auto rated, and NOT recommended on barrels shorter than 16 inches. A short barrel is not merely louder here — Banish says it puts extra wear straight into the first blast baffle.
steps.prose: The SPECS page widens the range downward as far as .17, so the low end is generous and the high end is the one that bites.
steps.quote: The BANISH 30 is rated up to .300 WBY MAG with a 24” barrel and is limited full auto rated. It is not recommended to use on barrels shorter than 16” as it may create more wear on the first blast baffle.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — INSTALLATION OF SUPPRESSOR, p.4
steps.warn: Ceiling .300 WBY MAG. Floor 16 inches of barrel.

steps.title: Rate of fire — 20 rounds a minute is the wear line
steps.action: Do not treat limited full-auto rated as unlimited. Banish puts the number at 20 rounds fired rapidly, meaning in under a minute, and says exceeding it causes premature baffle wear. Let the can cool between strings rather than counting on the titanium to absorb it.
steps.prose: A .30 can holds a lot of heat and 14.3 oz of titanium is not much of a heat sink. The wear happens whether or not anything looks wrong afterwards.
steps.caution: Let it cool between rapid-fire strings.
steps.quote: Firing more than 20 rounds rapid fire (less than one minute) will cause premature wear on the baffles.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — INSTALLATION OF SUPPRESSOR, p.4

steps.title: Check the seat before you ever fire it — and again before you strip it
steps.action: Look at the joint between the barrel shoulder and the face of the suppressor's thread mount. There must be NO visible gap: the mount has to be fully shouldered, and any crush washer left over from a muzzle brake must have been removed. A gap means the can is not concentric with the bore.
steps.prose: This is the single check that separates a suppressor that shoots where the rifle points from one that eats its own baffles.
steps.quote: Check the fit between your barrel and silencer before firing! The thread mount must be fully shouldered on the barrel.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: If there is any gap DO NOT fire the host with the silencer attached.

steps.title: Let it cool, or wear something
steps.action: After firing, the can is hot enough to burn through a bare grip. Banish tells you to use extreme caution, and offers a Devour suppressor cover or gloves as the way to handle it. The tube is where the heat is and the tube is where your hand has to go to unthread it.
steps.prose: The same warning appears again in the installation section, aimed at anyone retightening a hot can mid-string.
steps.quote: When removing the silencer, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Cover or gloves. Titanium does not look hot.

steps.title: Unthread the Banish 30 off the muzzle
steps.action: With the host clear and the can cool, turn the suppressor counter-clockwise off the 5/8x24 barrel threads. It went on hand tight — Banish says hand tighten only — so it should come off the same way. If it will not, it is because a direct thread can tightens itself under fire, not because it needs a wrench on the tube.
steps.prose: Banish also wants this joint checked constantly in use: after the first 5 discharges and every 30 thereafter. A can that walks loose is the mechanism behind most baffle strikes.
steps.caution: Hand tighten only. Never wrench a direct-thread Banish onto the barrel.
steps.quote: We recommend checking the security of the attachment after 5 discharges of the firearm and every 30 discharges thereafter.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — WARNING, p.2

steps.title: Protect the muzzle threads the moment the can is off
steps.action: Once the suppressor is off, fit a thread protector or another muzzle device over the bare 5/8x24 threads before the rifle goes in a case. Banish makes the point specifically for storage and transport, and it is about the crown as much as the thread — a dinged crown is an accuracy problem the can will then be blamed for.
steps.prose: Clean the threads at the same time. It is the only moment they are accessible.
steps.quote: Once the silencer is removed from the host firearm, BANISH recommends using a thread protector or other muzzle device to protect the muzzle threads and crown during storage or transport.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — WARNING, p.2

steps.title: Never fire an obstructed can
steps.action: Before it goes back on, sight through the bore of the suppressor and confirm nothing is in it — mud, dirt, a patch, standing solvent. Banish states the rule flatly. A .30 can with a blocked exit turns the next round into a pressure event inside a 1.5 inch titanium tube.
steps.prose: This matters most after a deep clean, because a soaked can that has not fully drained is an obstructed can.
steps.quote: Silencers must be free of obstructions such as mud, dirt, etc. DO NOT attempt to shoot through an obstructed silencer.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Look through it every single time.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The Banish 30 is off the barrel and the threads are protected — that is the routine strip. Everything further is the Deep Clean, and Banish sets the trigger at every 50 to 100 rounds fired. It also warns off one ammunition class entirely: solid lead or plated lead bullets are not recommended in this can.
steps.prose: That interval is short for a centrefire can, and it exists because the deep clean is the only way to reach the six baffles in the main tube.
steps.aside: Quoted as the text extraction renders it — the printed page shows the range as 50 - 100 and the hyphen is dropped by the extraction.
steps.quote: It is recommended that the suppressor be cleaned every 50 100 rounds fired. The use of solid lead or plated lead bullets is not recommended.
steps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.8

deepSteps.title: End cap off with the tool key and a T-45 torx
deepSteps.action: With the can off the rifle and the rifle unloaded, fit the supplied tool key and a T-45 torx wrench and unscrew the end cap. Banish suggests permanently bonding the torx wrench and the tool key together with JB Weld so they cannot be used separately or lost separately — which is a hint about how awkward the two-part tool is on its own.
deepSteps.prose: Do not improvise a substitute here. The cap goes back at 110-120 inch pounds and a rounded tool interface makes that impossible to reach.
deepSteps.quote: Using the provided tool key and T-45 torx wrench, remove the end cap of the suppressor. For best results, we recommend permanently attaching the T-45 torx wrench and the tool key together. This can be done with “JB Weld” or similar product found at any local hardware store.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.8

deepSteps.title: Front module off the main tube
deepSteps.action: Unthread the front module from the main tube. That module is what makes this can 9 inches instead of 7, and it carries two of the eight baffles inside it. Keep those two separate from the rest — they are not interchangeable with the main-tube baffles.
deepSteps.prose: Banish is explicit about that later: the module's two baffles have no indexing tabs and no centre slot, and must never go in the main tube.
deepSteps.caution: Keep the module's two baffles physically separate from the main tube's six.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the front module from the main tube.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.8

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The muzzle-threaded end of the main tube stays put
deepSteps.action: Do not attempt to remove the rear, barrel-threaded end of the main tube. Banish states it cannot be removed. That end carries the 5/8x24 threads and the datum the whole baffle stack indexes against; there is no published way to take it off and nothing to gain by trying.
deepSteps.prose: Everything you need to clean is reachable from the front once the end cap and module are off.
deepSteps.quote: The muzzle threaded end of the suppressor on the main tube cannot be removed.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.8

deepSteps.title: Soak for 24 hours, then push the baffles out
deepSteps.action: Spray your solvent of choice through the inside of the suppressor and leave it for a full 24 hours before trying to move anything. Then push the baffles out with a wooden dowel or the optional Baffle Removal Tool. The soak is what makes the push possible — forcing a dry stack is how baffles get scored.
deepSteps.prose: Wooden dowel, not steel rod. The baffles are titanium and the tube's inner wall is the surface everything indexes against.
deepSteps.caution: 24 hours of soak before any force is applied.
deepSteps.quote: Push baffles out of the tube with our Baffle Removal Tool (sold separately) or a wooden dowel.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.8

deepSteps.title: Eight baffles — six from the tube, two from the module
deepSteps.action: Count them out and keep the two groups apart: six baffles from the main tube and two from the front module. Scrub each one and the inside of the tube with a stiff brass or nylon brush and solvent or carbon killer, then make sure every part is clean and that no solvent is left standing anywhere.
deepSteps.prose: Banish's own warning is that care must be taken when reassembling, and it means the split. Two module baffles in the main tube will not index.
deepSteps.quote: The suppressor has eight baffles, six in the main tube and two in the front module. Care must be taken when reassembling. Use a stiff bristle brush (brass or nylon) with solvent / carbon killer of choice to clean the baffles and inside the tube. Make sure all parts are clean and solvent has been removed.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLY, p.8
deepSteps.warn: Solvent left inside the can is an obstruction.

deepSteps.title: Restack — six baffles, then the expansion spacer last
deepSteps.action: On a flat surface stack six matching baffles on each other and put the expansion spacer LAST on the stack. Every indexing tab has to be aligned and fully engaged in the baffle below it and in the spacer. Then slide the tube down over the stack, take it to the edge of the table and push the baffles up the tube with one finger.
deepSteps.prose: The expansion spacer does not have to come out for cleaning at all — but if it has, it goes back on the end of the stack, not in the middle.
deepSteps.quote: Using a flat surface, stack six matching baffles on top of each other, placing the expansion spacer last on the baffle stack. Make sure the indexing tabs are aligned and fully engaged in each corresponding baffle and expansion spacer.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — ASSEMBLY - FULL LENGTH 7”, p.6

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The module's two baffles never go in the main tube
deepSteps.action: When you rebuild the 9 inch configuration, keep the module's pair where they belong. Banish says these two have no indexing tabs and no centre slot and must only be used in the modular extension. Putting one in the main tube means the stack cannot index, and the end cap will tell you so by sitting proud.
deepSteps.prose: This is the one mistake this can invites, because all eight baffles look broadly alike in a tray.
deepSteps.quote: The module extension has two baffles, note these two baffles don’t have the indexing tabs or center slot and must only be used in the modular extension and never placed in the main tube.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — ASSEMBLY - FULL LENGTH 9”, p.5
deepSteps.warn: No indexing tab means module only.

deepSteps.title: End cap on — the 1/32 inch tell, then 110-120 inch pounds
deepSteps.action: Apply anti-seize to the threads, start the end cap and tighten it LIGHTLY first. With the baffles properly aligned only the 45 degree bevel on the cap will show, roughly 1/32 of an inch. If more than that is exposed the tabs are not indexed and the cap must come off — do not torque it. Once it sits right, finish to 110 to 120 inch pounds.
deepSteps.prose: That exposed bevel is a genuine go/no-go gauge for the whole internal stack, and it is the only one this can gives you.
deepSteps.quote: Lightly tighten the end cap, when the baffles are properly aligned only the 45 degree bevel on the end cap will be exposed (approximately 1/32”). If more than 1/32” is exposed the tabs on the baffles are not properly aligned.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 30 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — no revision or part number appears in this document — ASSEMBLY - FULL LENGTH 7”, p.6
deepSteps.warn: Finish tightening end cap to 110 - 120 inch pounds — never torque a misaligned stack.

cleaning.name: BAFFLES AND TUBE
tasks: Soak the inside with solvent for 24 hours before pushing anything out
Push the baffles out with a wooden dowel or the Baffle Removal Tool — never a steel rod
Scrub baffles and tube interior with a stiff brass or nylon brush
Keep the main tube's six baffles and the front module's two in separate groups
Confirm all solvent has been removed before reassembly

cleaning.name: END CAP AND THREADS
tasks: Apply anti-seize to the threads before the end cap goes on
Use the supplied tool key with a T-45 torx — consider bonding the two together
Check the 1/32 inch bevel tell before applying any torque

cleaning.name: MUZZLE INTERFACE
tasks: Clean the 5/8x24 barrel threads while the can is off
Confirm no crush washer is left on the barrel from a previous muzzle device
Fit a thread protector or muzzle device for storage and transport
Re-check the can's tightness after 5 discharges and every 30 thereafter

cleaning.name: SCHEDULE AND AMMUNITION
tasks: Do not use solid lead or plated lead bullets in this can
Allow the can to cool between rapid-fire strings; 20 rounds inside a minute is the stated wear line

reassembly: Stack six matching baffles with every indexing tab aligned and engaged, and place the expansion spacer last on the stack.
Slide the tube over the stack, take it to the edge of the table and push the baffles up the tube with a finger.
Flip the assembly so the open end is up and apply anti-seize to the threads before the end cap or modular end goes on.
For the 9 inch build, load the modular extension with its OWN two baffles — the ones without indexing tabs or a centre slot — and never put them in the main tube.
Tighten the end cap lightly, confirm only the 45 degree bevel shows at about 1/32 inch, then finish to 110 to 120 inch pounds.
Thread the can back onto the 5/8x24 muzzle hand tight only, with no gap at the shoulder.
fncheck: With the Banish 30 rebuilt, check the end cap shows only its 45 degree bevel at roughly 1/32 inch — more than that means the baffle stack is not indexed and the can is not safe to fire. Sight through the bore and confirm one clear channel with no step and no solvent left standing. On the rifle, confirm the mount is fully shouldered with no visible gap, then re-check tightness after the first 5 rounds and every 30 thereafter.
